solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: State of coalminer working around bottom of mine

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap themselves about the single letter
working suggests the letters of coalminer are set going in a new order
the bottom of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of mine is taken

explanation.surface: A remark about the condition a miner is in after his shift down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns COALMINER into CEREMONIAL less one E; 'around' wraps that round E, the last letter of 'mine' ('bottom of').
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, state describes formal official occasions, as in a state banquet, which are ritual and formal.

clue.text: Hot work following cold slice of meat

indicators.note: following puts the first pieces after the single letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: cook it hot after keeping it chilled, then carve.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a thick cut of meat, often pork or lamb, including a rib.

clue.text: Stopped umpire getting pelted

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is an umpire
rained means pelted, as in blows rained down

explanation.surface: A match called off when the umpire was hit by missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopped' suggests halting a game, but means held back from doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to stop yourself from doing something, so refrained means stopped.

clue.text: At sea, entered marina leaving sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sailor who came into a harbour and then left again for open water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean is the large sea between southern Europe and North Africa.

clue.text: Retribution in relation with English people backed

indicators.note: backed says the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: sis, short for sister, is a relation
men means people

explanation.surface: Payback involving a family member and some English folk who supported them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SIS + E + MEN into one backwards run.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is the Greek goddess of vengeance, and her name is used for deserved punishment.

clue.text: First-class study occupied by husband and idiot

parts.note: A1 is first-class, with the figure 1 shown as the letter I

indicators.note: occupied by says the following letter sits inside the word

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A top student whose study is taken over by a spouse, plus a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is a slang term for a silly, empty-headed person, so an idiot.

clue.text: Find fault in vehicle parking

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a car left in a parking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain or nitpick pettily, a direct synonym for finding fault.

clue.text: Shock of member supporting a Labour leader

indicators.note: supporting in a down answer places the piece underneath the others
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A politician's arm propping up the head of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: A Labour leader is a party head, but 'leader' only picks L from 'Labour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or dismay, so a shock.

clue.text: Used to hold her in sleep when upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clutching a partner who is restless in the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehensile tail or limb is adapted for grasping, as a monkey's tail grips branches.

clue.text: Killed repeatedly in the past, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word must be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: oft is an old word for often or repeatedly, and -ed is the past-tense ending, giving a mock word oft-ed

explanation.surface: A grim note that someone was murdered over and over in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful coinage OFT-ED ('done often in the past') said aloud matches the slang past tense of 'off', to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To off someone is slang for murdering them, so offed is a slang past tense for killed.

clue.text: Preserve from damage caused absorbing nearly everything

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: absorbing says one piece soaks up another and holds it inside

parts.note: made means caused, as in made trouble

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A jam-maker's advice that preserves can be ruined by drawing everything in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb, to save from damage, but is the noun: a jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, and a preserve is fruit conserved in sugar.

clue.text: Dancing cancan with tempo I'm backing

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are set in motion

explanation.surface: A dancer performing the cancan in time with the music behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads as reversing, but it is the definition, the music behind a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Accompaniment is the musical backing that supports a soloist or singer.

clue.text: Performer from start is teasing

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A stage act that teases the audience right from the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'stART IS TEasing'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, such as a singer or dancer, so a performer.

clue.text: Go through European valley

parts.note: to comb is to search through thoroughly

explanation.surface: An invitation to walk across a valley somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short narrow valley or hollow on a hillside, a word found in southern English place names.

clue.text: Breathing in desire

definitions.meaning: in phonetics and medicine the drawing of breath into the lungs, or a breathy sound
a hope or ambition to achieve something

explanation.definitionFit: Aspiration is both the act of drawing breath and a strong ambition or longing.

clue.text: Women from Essen or Asuncion? Probably Asuncion

indicators.note: from says the answer is lifted out of the place names that follow

explanation.surface: A question whether the ladies come from a German city or the Paraguayan capital, answered in favour of the latter.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'esSEN OR ASuncion'. The closing aside notes that Spanish-speaking ladies are likelier from Asuncion, Paraguay's capital, than from Essen in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Senoras is the Spanish for married ladies or madams, the plural of the title for a married woman.

clue.text: Sups second after embracing maiden in 'Twilight'

indicators.note: after places the single letter behind the rest
embracing says one piece hugs another inside it

parts.note: to sup is to eat an evening meal, so sups means dines
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A diner at a vampire-film night eating seconds while cuddling a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twilight' in quotes suggests the vampire novels, but it simply means half-light.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the faint light at dusk, so dimness, a lack of brightness, fits.

clue.text: Former wife petitioned, it's reported

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
pressed means urged or petitioned, as in pressed for reform

explanation.surface: Gossip that someone's ex-wife has filed a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To report something is to state or put it into words, which is what expressed means.

clue.text: Fashionable girl in a state

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
Diana is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A trendy young woman in a nervous fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' reads as being agitated, but 'in' is just a link and 'a state' is a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Group of jumbos fine without head

indicators.note: without head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: hairline means very fine, as in a hairline crack

explanation.surface: A herd of elephants doing fine except for a missing leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbos' suggests elephants; they are jumbo jets. 'without head' drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company operating a fleet of aircraft, such as jumbo jets.

clue.text: Cut skin cell evenly with this?

definitions.text: Cut skin cell evenly with this?

parts.note: to scalp is to cut away the skin of the head

indicators.note: evenly picks the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A surgeon's question about the right tool for a neat incision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes the even letters of 'cell', E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small sharp surgical knife used for precise incisions in skin.

clue.text: Secretly bring in non-wizard joining Hogwarts finally

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: a muggle, in the Harry Potter books, is a person without magic powers

explanation.surface: A non-magical person sneaking into the wizard school in the Harry Potter stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To smuggle is to bring goods or people in secretly and illegally.

clue.text: Topless model, substantial …

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a sample is a specimen or representative model of a product

explanation.surface: A glamour shot of a well-built model, trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the next clue's stripper scene; the clues are independent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or large, so substantial in size or amount.

clue.text: Mail perhaps with rubbish on Queen

indicators.note: on in a down answer places the first piece above the second

parts.note: pap is worthless or trivial reading matter, so rubbish
ER is the abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Junk post arriving on the monarch's doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like post, but is the Daily Mail, a British newspaper; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Mail is an example of a newspaper, which is a daily paper.

clue.text: … portion of stripper out in erotic performance

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, part of a striptease show.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'strippeR OUT IN Erotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a set sequence of moves in a show, so a performance.

clue.text: 'Friend' everybody, an unknown number

parts.note: all means everybody
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A greeting to everyone as friends, plus an algebra puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or partner, a synonym for a friend.

clue.text: Checking about end of aileron in the air

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round another

parts.note: impeding means checking or holding back

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of aileron

explanation.surface: A pilot inspecting the wing flap while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPEDING goes 'about' N, the last letter of 'aileron'. 'in the air' looks like flying but means about to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the air is sensed as coming soon, which is what impending means.

clue.text: Stand at the front of the class

definitions.text: Stand at the front of the class

parts.words: Stand at the front of the class
parts.note: reads like an order to a pupil, but describes the frame a teacher props a board on

explanation.surface: A teacher telling a pupil to come up to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame holding a board or canvas, often found at the front of a classroom.

clue.text: Described by median or mean?

indicators.note: described by means held within the outline of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A statistician asking which average best expresses the typical value.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'mediaN OR Mean'; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a typical or average standard, the sort of figure a median or mean expresses.

clue.text: Player teed off time and again

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and are out of order

explanation.surface: A golfer who teed off once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teed off' looks like a golf stroke, but 'off' is the anagram signal for PLAYER TEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Time and again means over and over, a synonym for repeatedly.
